newsitem.title: JAPAN: HANDBALL-RUSSIA AND SWEDEN ADVANCE TO MEN'S WORLD FINAL.
newsitem.headline: HANDBALL-RUSSIA AND SWEDEN ADVANCE TO MEN'S WORLD FINAL.

text.p: A goal by Serguei Pogorelov with three seconds of overtime left gave Russia a 25-24 victory over defending champions France in the semifinals of the men's world handball championship on Saturday.
The victory put Russia into Sunday's final against Sweden, who beat Hungary 31-19.
"In the end luck was on the Russian side," said Russia's coach Vladimir Maximov. "We never expected a match-up like that to be easy."

The Russian drive was led by Valeri Gopine with seven goals and Vassili Koudinov with six, including a bottom right seven-metre goal that tied the match with 1:47 left in the overtime period at Kumamoto City Gymnasium.

The Russian defence was stingy with goalkeepers Andrei Lavrov and Pavel Sukossian combining for 16 saves in 40 attempts and the rest of the team using their height advantage to dampen France's attack.
French coach Daniel Costantini said he had not expected his team to hold up as well as they did against the taller Russians.

"We were resigned to the fact that we would not be able to go over the top, so the only choice left was to go around them," Costantini told a news conference. "On the whole, that strategy worked well."
Russia led France 14-12 at halftime and kept the lead until 11:23 in the second half when Guillaume Gille levelled the score with a left nine-metre shot, one of his six goals of the evening.
The remaining minutes of regulation play featured a see-saw battle with crowd-pleaser Jackson Richardson scoring a fast break with 18 seconds left to keep France alive at 21-21.
Stephane Stoecklin led the French team with eight goals.
Sweden had an easier time in their match at Park Dome, Kumamoto, grabbing the lead at 14:36 in the first half on a upper right nine-metre shot by Steffan Olsson and then never losing it.
Sweden's Stefan Loevgren scored seven goals and Pierre Thorsson four. Six other Swedes had three goals each.
It was not all bad news for the Hungarian offence, however, as Jozsef Eles scored 10 goals in 11 attempts.
